Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll begin with the workspace contract in `README.md`. Then I’ll use the wake-visual inspection skill to read both rollout views and the fish-control bookshelf skill at the required transfer point before proposing or editing the single candidate.

The workspace confirms that CFD must not be run here and that the candidate must remain continuously valid. I’m now reading both applicable skill contracts in full; their required references will determine the evidence-inspection sequence and the allowable mechanism transfer.

The visual skill requires an anchored comparison between the best finite trajectory and the most informative failure, with metrics and diagnostics—not image impressions alone. I’ll inventory the sampled evidence and inherited logs, then select those cases from their score/termination data before opening both visual rows.

All four sampled rollouts are valid direct-uniform still-water captures, so there is no termination failure in this sample. I’ll treat the lowest-score/slowest useful trajectory as the informative mechanism underperformer, not fabricate a failed termination. Next I’m comparing milestone, path, load, command, and rate-limit behavior to identify which policy difference actually explains the ranking.

I’m applying the wake-visual skill now: opening the combined top-down vorticity and oblique Lambda2 sheets for the best sampled controller and the slowest captured underperformer. The visual read will be checked against their `15.60T` versus `16.09T` arrival and `1.794L` versus `1.822L` distance integrals.

The two-view evidence shows the same useful physical class in both cases: self-propelled motion from a quiescent release, a coherent alternating wake, productive targetward translation, and no collision/exit/instability precursor. The distinction is trajectory efficiency rather than wake existence—the faster case reaches the target on a slightly tighter, earlier approach. I’m now isolating the controller mechanism differences and inherited optimizer rationale before choosing one architecture change.

The inherited parent adds a newer evaluated hybrid that is directly relevant: per-joint full-demand previews retained capture and scored `0.08633`, nearly matching the `0.08781` common full-demand leader. I’m incorporating that rollout—not merely its proposal—by inspecting its two-view sheet and extracting the same path/load/rate metrics before deciding whether the hybrid lesson survives.

The inherited hybrid’s evaluated result survives as a real lesson: per-joint full-demand sensing matches the common guard’s fast class (`15.593T` vs `15.604T`) while reducing path and peak load (`13.017L`, `0.03798/0.01853` vs `13.137L`, `0.04226/0.02076`). Because the protocol permits optional later consultation and this is an architecture iteration, I’m consulting the primitive catalog now for one compact mechanism that addresses the remaining early-turn/path tradeoff; I will not copy gains or kinematics.

The catalog’s relevant invariant is posteriorly lagged traveling-wave propulsion: an anterior steering/rate event should not automatically suppress the posterior joint when that joint still has rate margin. I’m reading the cited source-family notes because this invariant will inform the edit; the resulting policy will translate only joint-local normalized state and demand, not any published gain, phase, cadence, or route.

I’ve selected one mechanism, not a gain sweep: start from the evaluated per-joint full-demand hybrid and make the unfulfilled-redirect carrier guard joint-local as well. The current code still lets one joint’s near-envelope redirect gate suppress both joints; the hypothesis is that preserving posterior rhythmic authority when only the anterior joint is constrained will retain the fast capture class while reducing unnecessary path/load coupling. Per the visual skill, I’m recording this diagnosis and falsification in the candidate notes before touching the solver.

The candidate-specific note is now in place, including the required bookshelf transfer block. I’m updating the durable experience bank with the evaluated hybrid result: it resolves the previous “next test” into a reusable sensing-versus-allocation lesson and records the speed/path/load boundary without claiming this new candidate’s unevaluated behavior.

I’m now applying the single solver edit. It preserves the inherited hybrid’s full-demand per-joint preview and changes only carrier allocation under an unresolved body-frame redirect: separate head/tail redirect guards and reversal scales, with steering untouched and no gain or schema changes.

The solver now contains one candidate with the intended architecture and unchanged parameter schema. I’m checking the exact diff against the evaluated hybrid to ensure no scaffold drift, then I’ll run static contract checks and the required dedicated check-runner; no CFD will be launched.

The local Julia executable is unavailable, so the direct policy smoke test cannot run in this workspace; no CFD was attempted. I’m invoking the required dedicated check-runner now to validate the parameter schema, policy restrictions, notes, and material guidance change without simulation.

The independent static scan passes: 37 declared parameters cover all 36 direct references, the public functions and two-action return are present, delimiters balance, all three required files are nonempty, the guidance differs materially from its assigned parent, and no prohibited hidden-time/route/I/O tokens were found. I’m waiting for the required contract checker’s independent verdict.

The first checker report was internally inconsistent—it described the updated hypothesis but mistakenly claimed the already-present notes and guidance still needed updates, and it cited the prefill score as “strongest” despite the sampled `0.08781` result. Per the workspace contract, I’m rerunning the same checker with explicit current-file and parent-diff verification so it returns an actual pass/fail verdict.

The rerun failed only because that checker exhausted its own audit window, not because it found a contract defect. I’m invoking a fresh check-runner for the required end-to-end live-filesystem audit, with the scope reduced to the deterministic checks so it can produce the mandated verdict.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

The candidate uses joint-local redirect guards so one joint’s envelope pressure does not suppress the other joint’s carrier authority. Static schema validation found 37 declared fields, 36 direct references, and none missing. The boundary check passed; no CFD was run.

The formal checker could not fully pass because the rendered `README.md` contains the same assigned-parent marker twice, and Julia is unavailable. These are pre-existing workspace/tooling issues; manual material-guidance and schema checks passed.
